feedback: No earlier race exists, so this feedback rests only on the contract and on what I had to set in the controller for this geometry, not on any measured outcome. Five sensors at 0.015 m spacing with 12 mm footprints overlap the 25 mm tape, so at least one sensor sees tape through a moderate lateral error, which is why I used linear weights (+1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1) and kp 3.0. If the next race shows steering_oscillation high with line_loss_events at 0 (the robot weaving on the line), reduce kp or raise kd, and keep the sensor spacing. If it shows line_loss_events above zero, concentrated on the sharpest slalom bends, the outer sensors at ±0.03 m are not reaching the tape early enough. Try a wider span or a larger forward offset (y up to about 0.07 m) so the signal is read before the wheels turn. If completion_time is near or above 3 s with no line losses, the wheel track or mass is limiting turn authority, not the sensors. Try a shorter wheel track (0.10 m) to raise turn rate, keeping the mass near 0.7 kg, since yaw inertia depends on body size and mass.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events > 0 on the slalom or s-bend, try a forward offset of y = 0.07 m for all five sensors (keep x positions and sensor_size 0.012) to give earlier bend anticipation. No earlier race evidence yet; this is a hypothesis to test.

If steering_oscillation is high on the oval with few line losses, keep the sensor geometry but ask for a lower-gain controller path by reporting whether a sensor spacing of 0.02 m (x = ±0.04, ±0.02, 0) gives a smoother signal. No earlier race evidence yet.
If completion_time is above 2.8 s with no line losses, reduce wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m to increase turn rate on the slalom while keeping mass at 0.7 kg. No earlier race evidence yet.
